posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Suggestion for you:

Pick an agent for work, and pick an agent for personal.

You could explore to do this all with Grok Bot (with many different types of bots)

Personally, I like @bot for work, and @Muse for personal agents.

It helps to create a clean separation for me.

Here are some reasons why Grok for Work:

- Grok is very good at coding, so if you want your bot to help you do engineering / building, Grok beats muse.

- Groks VM / Browser is very strong. I love it for deeper tasks that are work releated.

- Groks integration with X is goated. And I use X heavily for work.

Here are some reasons why @Muse for personal: 

- The simplicity with one agent who knows all is awesome

- The pricing is either free, or very cheap

- They have a history of keeping your private data safe

- They are focused on building personal agents, including training their models this way

- It gives me enough permissions to control my agents at the personal level 

- Building personal software within the app is so easy and well suited for personal use cases 

- Meta is all in on personal agents, which means significant resources being poured into product advancements (your agent gets better every day)

- Muse SDK allowing my agent to go with me on many devices is the right direction

- Meta's Sunglasses gets way more interesting once Muse is supported.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
I built a @Grok @Bot that watches $SPCX on its own — fully automated, no manual work.

I’ve been running it for over a month and fine-tuned it several times. This version is very good.

Every weekday before the market opens, it scans filings, analyst moves, insider buying, X sentiment, Starlink licenses, and space policy. Then it posts a fixed-format brief with links to every source.

Swap the ticker you like or add as many tickers as you wanted → $TSLA, $INTC, $NVDA and others. Same bot, new target.

What this Bot will do: 

•  ⁠Monitors NASDAQ:SPCX (SpaceX) every weekday before market open

•  ⁠Fixed-format morning brief, even on quiet days

•  ⁠Tracks filings: 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 13D, 13F, Form 4

•  ⁠Analyst upgrades, downgrades, and price target changes

•  ⁠Insider buying clusters and named 13F moves

•  ⁠X discussion volume and sentiment spikes

•  ⁠Official posts from @elonmusk, @SpaceX, @spacexai, @grok, @bot

•  ⁠Starlink licenses and spectrum approvals worldwide

•  ⁠Space policy: NASA, Space Force, FCC, export controls

•  ⁠AI and data center news affecting SpaceX

•  ⁠Every item links back to its source

•  ⁠Reports stay in chat — no emails, no spam

https://x.ai/bot/awNIyq3TPG4tSKBPqyvO7

quote.text:
Some reasons Grok bot is better than a human employee:

• You can communicate super autistically (aka direct) and it won't think you're a jerk
• Won't report you to HR
• Doesn't browse X while working, unless it was part of the task
• You can literally watch its screen while it works and it won't get uncomfortable
• Is available, and can work 24/7
• Instant expertise on any subject
• Can read and understand 420,000 words per second
• Infinitely patient: won't roll its eyes or get mad if you ask for the 690th rewrite because you gave bad instructions
• Won't talk sht to your co workers when you give it a task a child could have done simply to liberate some mental bandwidth for other tasks
• Extremely high IQ
• Impeccable memory
• Faster learner
• Gets dramatically more capable daily
